page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.6xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical Intel Xeon 8369B cores running at 2.7 GHz. The system architecture is x86_64, supported by 48 GB of RAM, which yields a compute-focused memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on external storage solutions and network-attached volumes. Network connectivity is established with a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark data places the ecs.c7.6xlarge in the average performance tier across most standardized tests. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a single-core stress-ng score of 1884.19 and a multi-core score of 23298.44. In memory performance, it registers a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 1259.99 GB/sec and a large block uncached write bandwidth of 63.06 GB/sec. Notably, the instance demonstrates strong performance in text generation for small language models, reaching 298.93 tokens per second, while maintaining average speeds of 15.37 tokens per second for medium parameter models.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.c7.6xlarge is its lack of local SSD storage and GPU acceleration, which limits its utility for heavy data-science training or high-IOPS local database workloads. However, its dedicated CPU allocation and AVX-512 instruction support provide stable, predictable performance for compute-bound tasks. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio offers a resource-dense configuration for workloads that require high processing power without the overhead of excess memory. This makes the instance suitable for web serving, software compilation, multi-threaded decompression, and CPU-based inference tasks.
